title: I Made Spider-Man Swing Without Animating a Single Frame
why_read: A fun personal project showing how an LLM-driven Blender MCP server can automate 3D character animation for a promotional video, interesting as an applied AI tooling demo but lightweight on rigor.
analysis: The author describes using Blender's MCP server integration to let an AI assistant control a 3D animation tool and produce a Spider-Man-style swinging animation without manually keyframing it, as part of marketing content for their own code review product. It's a creative demonstration of AI-driven creative tooling, specifically how MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers let LLMs control complex professional software like Blender. The technical depth is modest, mostly a narrative of discovery rather than an analysis of underlying techniques, and it doubles as promotional content for an unrelated product.
